title: Make the ticket tier read policy check one event instead of every event
detail: Deep audit 2026-11-19. The event_ticket_types read policy was `event_id in (select events.id from public.events)`. Under a caller role that runs every events policy over every event to build the list, then checks one id, so each tier read grows with the event count: 18.7 ms per read at 531 events. It was the busiest statement in pg_stat_statements (558,482 calls, 32.9 ms mean, about five hours of database time). Fix: migration 20270346200000 recreates it as a correlated EXISTS on the one event by primary key (18.19 ms to 0.63 ms as anon on a copy, same rows). Visibility unchanged: both forms read events under the caller's RLS. Proved by supabase/tests/event_ticket_types_read_policy.test.sql. Follow-up not in this row: density_by_city and four calendar feeds still join a materialized time zone CTE (the SCAN-1210 swap to public.tz_zone_lookup), measured 295 ms to 21 ms for density_by_city.

verify.note: Fails on main: the last migration defines the policy as an IN over every event. Passes when the EXISTS form is the latest definition.
